Types of Bourdon Tube Compared: C Type, Spiral and Helical

Types of Bourdon tube are named after the shape of the hollow, flattened tube: C type, spiral and helical. All three work on the same principle. Pressure inside the tube makes it try to straighten, and the tip movement drives the pointer. The shape decides how much tip movement is produced and what pressure range the tube suits.

TypeTube shapePressure rangeKey feature
C typeSingle arc of about 250 to 270 degreesLow to mediumMost common, small tip travel amplified by sector gear and pinion
SpiralSeveral turns wound in one flat planeLower rangesLarger tip travel gives better sensitivity and accuracy
HelicalSeveral turns wound like a coil springVery high pressureLarge travel, good overpressure resistance

How to choose a Bourdon tube type

  1. Check the maximum working pressure and select a range so normal readings sit in the middle part of the dial.
  2. Use a C type for general plant service at low to medium pressure.
  3. Use a spiral type when fine resolution at low pressure is needed.
  4. Use a helical type for very high pressure or where overpressure can occur.
  5. Select a liquid filled case when there is vibration or pulsation.
  6. Pick a tube material such as brass, phosphor bronze or beryllium copper that suits the process fluid.

Spiral and helical tubes add more turns, so the total tip movement is the sum of the small movement of each turn. This is why they can drive the pointer with less gearing than a C type tube.
